expectations.text: The reply explains briefly why ranking individuals by AI acceptance rate and PRs merged misleads (for example it rewards volume and gaming and says nothing about value or quality).
expectations.evidence: "Both numbers measure activity, not value... It can rise while quality falls. PRs merged rewards small, frequent changes and punishes the people who review, mentor, fix incidents and delete code"; "People will optimise the number... engineers accept every suggestion and split every PR in two." Content clearly meets the assertion. The section is 251 words, about the same share of the reply as A's and C's critiques; overall length is judged under the last assertion.

expectations.text: The reply suggests raising it with the VP privately first, with questions and a concrete alternative such as team-level delivery measures (for example DORA metrics), rather than an open confrontation.
expectations.evidence: Step 1: "Ask questions privately first, not in a meeting... Ask the VP: What problem is this solving...? ... let him save face." Step 2: "Team-level DORA metrics (lead time, deployment frequency, change failure rate, recovery time)" plus review wait, WIP, DevEx survey and a Copilot comparison-group pilot.

expectations.text: The reply says that in the Netherlands a system for monitoring employees' performance needs the works council's consent (article 27 WOR), and suggests involving the works council if a private conversation doesn't work.
expectations.evidence: "It has a consent right (instemmingsrecht, art. 27(1)(l) WOR) on systems suited to monitoring or evaluating employees' behaviour or performance"; step 6: "If the VP hears you out and goes ahead anyway, the works council route and HR are the legitimate next channels, in proportion." Explicit fallback after the private conversation.

expectations.text: The reply routes concerns to the right channel and does not send a business disagreement to the confidential adviser (vertrouwenspersoon) or suggest leaks or sabotage.
expectations.evidence: Channels: VP privately, manager-led process with HR for individual concerns, OR, HR, then "independent advice (a union, or an employment lawyer) before escalating." No vertrouwenspersoon, no leaks or sabotage.

expectations.text: The reply helps the user protect themselves, for example by keeping a factual record and finding allies, without telling them to stay silent.
expectations.evidence: "Find allies with a stake... you don't need to lead any fight yourself"; "Put your points in writing, short and factual"; "Keep a factual record of what you asked and what the answers were"; "You are not obliged to risk your career." Does not tell the user to stay silent.

expectations.text: The reply is practical and short enough to act on, not a lecture (roughly 500 words or less).
expectations.evidence: 1057 words (wc -w), roughly double the 550 cap. Five evidence bullets, two Dutch-law bullets, six steps, a draft message and an assumptions paragraph: thorough, but not short enough to act on quickly.

factual_errors.evidence: Checked: Faros AI Productivity Paradox Report (July 2025): 10,000+ developers, 98% more PRs merged, 91% longer review time, 154% larger PRs, all correct (faros.ai). 1 - 0.9^10 = 0.651, correct. WOR art. 27(1)(l) and 50-employee threshold correct. Two imprecisions not counted as errors: (1) 'Acceptance rate measures how much of a suggestion someone keeps' loosely describes what is really the share of shown suggestions accepted; (2) 'Copilot's admin consoles often show per-person usage by default': per-seat last-activity data is visible to admins, and user-level usage data exists via the API, but the detailed usage-metrics policy launched off by default (GitHub changelog, Oct 2025). The claim is hedged with 'often'.

skill_leak.evidence: No mention of skills, reference files or internal jargon.

owns_result.evidence: The prompt describes a planned policy, not a bad outcome that has happened.

best_insight.value: The arithmetic that a random weekly bottom 10% would catch about 65% of engineers at least once in ten weeks makes the noise argument concrete and hard for the VP to wave away.
best_insight.evidence: 'about 65% of engineers land in it at least once in 10 weeks (1 - 0.9^10)'

suggestions.assertion: The reply says that in the Netherlands a system for monitoring employees' performance needs the works council's consent (article 27 WOR), and suggests involving the works council if a private conversation doesn't work.
suggestions.reason: Every sample cites art. 27(1)(l) WOR and the 50-employee threshold, so this does not discriminate. A sharper check: the reply does not assume a works council exists (many 50+ companies lack one) and says what to do if there is none (union, HR). Sample C states 'At 300 people you have a works council' as fact and would still pass.

suggestions.assertion: The reply routes concerns to the right channel and does not send a business disagreement to the confidential adviser (vertrouwenspersoon) or suggest leaks or sabotage.
suggestions.reason: Nearly trivially satisfied. A stricter version would require that any mention of the vertrouwenspersoon is limited to unwanted behaviour or integrity concerns. Sample C pairs 'the vertrouwenspersoon or your OR' as the next step 'if things turn hostile' without saying what each is for, and it passes only because 'hostile' plausibly means unwanted behaviour.

suggestions.assertion: The reply explains briefly why ranking individuals by AI acceptance rate and PRs merged misleads (for example it rewards volume and gaming and says nothing about value or quality).
suggestions.reason: 'Briefly' is not defined. Samples B and D spend 251 and 182 words on the critique (similar shares of their replies to A and C), so overall length is really tested by the last assertion. Either drop 'briefly' or give it a word cap.

No assertion checks factual accuracy of cited evidence (Faros, METR, arithmetic) or the GDPR/AVG angle, which three of four samples raise. A 'cited figures are correct and caveated' assertion would separate careful samples from ones that misstate numbers (e.g. C's '300 people, about 30 names' when only engineers are ranked).

eval_feedback.overall: 5/6: the most complete and well-evidenced advice, but at 1057 words it is roughly twice the length limit.
